stories.title: AI-Native Hanover Park Leases Full Floor at 387 Park Ave. South
stories.excerpt: A new lease with AI-native fund administrator Hanover Park and the expansion and extension of PMG Worldwide’s existing space have been recent highlights at TF Cornerstone’s 387 Park Ave. South, which has seen more than 100,000 square feet of leasing activity in the past year. The recent transactions follow K Health’s long-term renewal and the expansion of another TAMI user completed in late 2025. Hanover Park signed a lease for the building’s entire 10th floor, totaling approximately 19,269 square feet. PMG Worldwide renewed its lease on the entire second floor while expanding into the entire third floor, bringing its total footprint to approximately 38,744 square feet. “We’re pleased to welcome Hanover Park to 387 Park Avenue South and to expand our relationship with PMG Worldwide,” said Joe Lanzilotta, Director, Commercial Asset Management at TF Cornerstone. “The property continues to outperform the market as a destination for growing businesses.” The post AI-Native Hanover Park Leases Full Floor at 387 Park Ave. South appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hanover Park (AI fund admin) leased full 10th floor, 19,269 SF at 387 Park Ave South, Manhattan.
PMG Worldwide renewed and expanded to 38,744 SF across floors 2–3; 100,000 SF leased past year.
TAMI tenants (K Health, tech firms) driving office demand in Flatiron submarket.
stories.summary: TF Cornerstone's 387 Park Ave South in Manhattan has seen over 100,000 square feet of leasing activity in the past year, with AI-native firm Hanover Park signing a full-floor lease (19,269 SF) on the 10th floor and PMG Worldwide expanding its footprint to 38,744 SF. Recent activity follows K Health's 2025 renewal and another TAMI tenant expansion. The property continues to outperform the broader market.
stories.impact: Sustained demand from technology, AI, and media tenants in Manhattan's Flatiron/South Park Avenue submarket signals strong job-driven office occupancy, which supports demand for nearby multifamily (East Village, Gramercy, Union Square submarkets) and justifies premium rents. Continued tech employer hiring and office expansion reduces multifamily supply headwinds in adjacent residential neighborhoods.

stories.title: PMB, Loma Linda University Health Break Ground on Inpatient Rehab Hospital
stories.excerpt: PMB, a leading healthcare real estate developer, and Loma Linda University Health with Lifepoint Rehabilitation, a business unit of Lifepoint Health, recently broke ground on a new, 99,000-square-foot, 80-bed inpatient rehabilitation hospital in Redlands. Located at 11207 New Jersey., the three-story facility will function as a standalone hospital. “Breaking ground today represents far more than just laying the foundation for a new building – it’s a promise to the community,” said Nolan Weinberg, SVP of Development for PMB. “Inpatient rehabilitation is a critical bridge between acute medical recovery and returning to everyday life..” Loma Linda University Rehabilitation Hospital will be jointly operated by Loma Linda University Health and Lifepoint Rehabilitation and is anticipated to open in the summer of 2028. Upon completion, Loma Linda University Health will transition its existing inpatient rehabilitation unit to the new facility. PMB’s partners on the project include general contractor Layton Construction, architect Material Design Architects and financing partner Harrison Street Asset Management. The post PMB, Loma Linda University Health Break Ground on Inpatient Rehab Hospital appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: PMB & Loma Linda University Health broke ground on 80-bed inpatient rehab hospital in Redlands, CA.
99,000 SF, three-story facility opening summer 2028; Harrison Street Asset Management financing.
Healthcare employment and specialized facility draw workforce and caregiver/family in-migration to Inland Empire.
stories.summary: PMB and Loma Linda University Health broke ground on a 99,000-square-foot, 80-bed inpatient rehabilitation hospital in Redlands, California, to open summer 2028. The project is jointly operated by Loma Linda University Health and Lifepoint Rehabilitation, financed by Harrison Street Asset Management, and built by Layton Construction. The facility will relocate Loma Linda's existing inpatient rehab unit to the new standalone building.
stories.impact: Major healthcare infrastructure investment in Redlands/Inland Empire signals employer growth in the medical services sector, creating sustained demand for workforce housing and attracting healthcare professionals and families to the submarket. Multifamily developers should target Class B/C rental stock within 3–5 miles of the hospital and along major commute corridors to Loma Linda University campus.

stories.title: Astoria Favorite :3Coffee Roasters Expands to Halletts Point
stories.excerpt: The Durst Organization has signed :3Coffee Roasters to a 1,232-square-foot lease for a new retail location at 30 Halletts Point in Astoria, Queens. Expected to open later this year, the new shop marks an expansion for the family-owned business and its second Astoria location. It will also be the first retail at 20 and 30 Halletts Point, which opened last year with 647 apartments. “Halletts Point is a thriving community with spectacular views of Manhattan and Queens. As the neighborhood continues to grow, we are selecting retailers that will bring additional value to residents and neighbors alike, and we are excited to welcome :3Coffee Roasters,” said Jody Durst, President of The Durst Organization. :3Coffee Roasters was founded by Astoria residents Fabian Guzman and Andrea Gomez. The brand first opened on Steinway Street in Astoria and later expanded to the Flatiron District in Manhattan, building a following for their neighborhood-oriented approach and high-quality offerings. The Durst Organization was represented in-house by Karen Rose and Eric Engelhardt and by KSR’s Zach Nathan, Mark Gallucci, and Hunter Lazan. :3Coffee Roasters was represented by Genaro Otero at Sinvin. The post Astoria Favorite :3Coffee Roasters Expands to Halletts Point appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: :3Coffee Roasters (Astoria-based cafe) signed 1,232 SF lease at 30 Halletts Point, Queens.
First retail at mixed-use building with 647 apartments that opened last year in Astoria waterfront.
Neighborhood-oriented retailer signals placemaking maturity and retail demand stabilization in new multifamily nodes.
stories.summary: The Durst Organization signed :3Coffee Roasters, a family-owned Astoria coffee brand, to a 1,232-square-foot retail lease at 30 Halletts Point, marking the first retail activation at the mixed-use building that completed last year with 647 apartments. The location is :3Coffee's second Astoria site and will open later this year. The property offers Manhattan and Queens views on the waterfront.
stories.impact: Retail anchoring at new multifamily nodes (Halletts Point has 647 units) indicates resident density sufficient to support independent retailers and local services, reducing perceived isolation risk for developers in emerging waterfront submarkets. Success of neighborhood-oriented retail at Class A new construction validates demand fundamentals in Astoria/Long Island City and supports rental premium absorption for newer supply.

stories.title: CBRE Arranges Debt on Advanced Manufacturing Campus in San Jose’s Golden Triangle
stories.excerpt: CBRE announced it arranged $67.4 million in financing for Forge North First, a mixed-phase industrial/R&D campus and advanced manufacturing development in San Jose’s Golden Triangle submarket. Mike Walker, Brad Zampa, and Andy Gross of CBRE’s Debt & Structured Finance team in San Francisco arranged the five-year bridge loan with floating-rate, non-recourse financing from an institutional lender on behalf of Four Corners Properties and a West Coast-based institutional investor. “The combination of surging occupier demand and extremely limited supply positions Four Corners to create significant value at Forge North First,” said Zampa. Four Corners, an established local investor and developer founded in 2005, has invested in 50 buildings totaling 7.2 million square feet. In January 2026, Four Corners and its institutional partner acquired the existing 205,800-square-foot, five-building campus from BXP. The mixed-phase program includes comprehensive modernization of the existing campus and development of two advanced manufacturing buildings totaling approximately 239,000 square feet. The post CBRE Arranges Debt on Advanced Manufacturing Campus in San Jose’s Golden Triangle appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CBRE arranged $67.4M five-year bridge loan for Forge North First advanced manufacturing campus, San Jose Golden Triangle.
Four Corners Properties acquired 205,800 SF existing campus Jan 2026; adding 239,000 SF new manufacturing buildings.
Surging occupier demand and extremely limited supply position for value creation in San Jose industrial/R&D.
stories.summary: CBRE arranged a $67.4 million, five-year non-recourse bridge loan from an institutional lender for Forge North First, an advanced manufacturing and R&D campus in San Jose's Golden Triangle submarket. Four Corners Properties and a West Coast institutional investor acquired the existing 205,800-square-foot, five-building campus from BXP in January 2026 and are funding comprehensive modernization plus development of two new 239,000-square-foot advanced manufacturing buildings.
stories.impact: Strong occupier demand and tight industrial/advanced manufacturing supply in San Jose Golden Triangle signals sustained employment growth in semiconductor equipment, biotech, and advanced manufacturing—sectors that attract skilled, higher-wage workers to the Bay Area. Developers should prioritize multifamily near major employment nodes (Coyote Valley, North San Jose corridors) to capture worker in-migration ahead of facility completions; rents in adjacent submarkets will pressure upward.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Closes Sale of Downtown Westfield Mixed-Use
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap arranged the sale of 251 North Ave. W., a mixed-use property in Westfield, NJ, for $5,260,000. Alan Cafiero, David Cafiero and Damien Rance of Marcus & Millichap exclusively marketed the property on behalf of the seller and procured the private buyer. “Downtown Westfield continues to be one of the most desirable mixed-use investment markets in New Jersey,” said Alan Cafiero, senior managing director investments in Marcus & Millichap’s New Jersey office. “The combination of a premier downtown location, immediate proximity to the train station and a strong, diverse tenant roster generated significant investor interest in this asset.” The property is a three-story, 17,831-square-foot building on a 0.18-acre lot with direct access to municipal commuter parking. It has nine suites and was renovated in 2014. The rent roll features a diverse mix of service-oriented tenants, including Columbia Bank, Edward Jones, the State of New Jersey, BAYADA Home Health Care and Rooster Spin. The post Marcus & Millichap Closes Sale of Downtown Westfield Mixed-Use appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap sold 251 North Ave W, mixed-use Westfield NJ, for $5.26M; 17,831 SF, nine suites.
Prime downtown location, direct access to commuter rail, diverse service-oriented tenant roster (Columbia Bank, Edward Jones, State of NJ, BAYADA).
Westfield downtown continues strong mixed-use investment demand; renovated 2014, high occupancy.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap brokered the sale of 251 North Ave W., a three-story, 17,831-square-foot mixed-use property in Westfield, New Jersey, for $5.26 million. The 0.18-acre property features nine suites with a diverse tenant mix including Columbia Bank, Edward Jones, the State of New Jersey, BAYADA Home Health Care, and Rooster Spin; it sits near the commuter rail station with direct municipal parking access and was renovated in 2014.
stories.impact: Westfield's downtown mixed-use market remains competitive and stable, underpinned by strong commuter rail connectivity to Manhattan and stable institutional tenant demand. Nearby multifamily inventory should benefit from the reliable transit access and downtown employment base; limited suburban NJ mixed-use supply maintains high barriers to entry, supporting values in complementary residential assets within walkable radius.

stories.title: Nuveen Green Capital Closes $281M C-PACE Loan for Boston Condos
stories.excerpt: The steady climb of commercial property assessed clean energy (C-PACE) financing around the U.S. has made its way to one of Boston’s tallest buildings. Millennium Partners has secured a $281 million C-PACE loan to implement energy efficiency upgrades at the 62-story Winthrop Center in Downtown Boston, the developer announced Friday afternoon. Nuveen Green Capital originated the fixed-rate loan under the Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) Massachusetts program which marked the largest C-PACE financing to date in the New England region, according to the lender.,. The condo inventory of the roughly 800,000 square-foot mixed-use building completed in 2023 attracted strong lender competition with many debt funds chasing the loan, according to a source familiar with the transaction. The C-PACE debt closed concurrently with a $575 million commercial mortgage backed securities (CMBS) loan led by Morgan Stanley for the office and retail portion of the tower according to a presale report from Moody’s. CoStar first reported the MP Trust 2026-WTRP single-asset-single-borrower deal for Boston’s largest building in the city’s financial district. The combined $856 million debt package takes out a prior construction loan from Cale Street in October 2020 after the London firm stepped in following another bank who backed out during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, according to sources. “We were honored to partner with MassDevelopment to recapitalize the largest C-PACE-financed project in New England, one that has helped reshape downtown Boston with state-of-the-art, energy-efficient residences,” Mike Doty, senior director of originations for NGC, said in a statement. Christopher M. Jeffries, founder of Millennium Partners, said in a statement that the C-PACE loan “recognizes the investments we have made in energy efficiency while providing long-term capital that supports the building’s enduring performance.” The PACE Massachusetts program was updated in June
bullets: Nuveen Green Capital closed $281M C-PACE loan for Winthrop Center (62-story, 800,000 SF condo tower, Boston), largest New England C-PACE.
Millennium Partners financing energy efficiency upgrades; concurrent $575M CMBS loan led by Morgan Stanley for office component.
C-PACE debt competition and fixed-rate availability signal strong condo market and capital appetite for residential mixed-use.
stories.summary: Nuveen Green Capital originated a $281 million fixed-rate C-PACE loan for Millennium Partners to fund energy efficiency upgrades at Winthrop Center, a 62-story, roughly 800,000-square-foot mixed-use building in Downtown Boston completed in 2023. The loan, the largest C-PACE financing to date in New England, closed alongside a $575 million CMBS loan led by Morgan Stanley for the office component. Strong lender competition for the condo inventory indicated robust capital demand.
stories.impact: Successful large-scale C-PACE refinancing at a completed Boston condo tower signals strong capital availability for residential mixed-use in major markets and validates energy-efficient multifamily assets as attractive to institutional debt funds. Developers should examine C-PACE and blended financing strategies (C-PACE + CMBS) for new multifamily with efficiency features; abundant capital chasing these deals may compress spreads but improves project feasibility in high-cost markets like Boston.

stories.title: Nalcorp, Clipper Equity Buy Coney Island Oceanfront Development Site for $20M
stories.excerpt: Fancy a trip to the Boardwalk? A pair of New York-based real estate development and investment firms — Nalcorp and Clipper Equity — have acquired a land parcel at 2015 Boardwalk West, an oceanfront development in Coney Island, Brooklyn, from seller Bath Site LLC for $20 million, broker TerraCRG announced Friday. The parking lot property, which spans 69,530 square feet and has 247 feet of Boardwalk frontage, seems to be part of a larger ongoing development on the site. Permits were filed in 2024 to build a 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use building at 2015 Boardwalk West. The larger parcel of land home to the development was purchased in 2006 by the City Investment Fund — a real estate private equity vehicle launched by the Fisher Brothers and Morgan Stanley — from Thor Equities for $90 million. Following the 2006 sale, the larger parcel was subdivided into six separate tax lots, including the one part of this most recent transaction, which is called Block 7072, Lot 6. Bath Site LLC — an entity comprising Georgica Green Ventures and its nonprofit partner RiseBoro Community Partnership — acquired this property in July 2024 for $10.4 million. Dan Marks and Daniel Lebor from TerraCRG represented Bath Site LLC in this transaction. The firm did not disclose the names of the brokers who represented the buyers. The buyers did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment, while the seller could not be reached for comment. “Coney Island has become one of New York City’s most exciting waterfront growth stories,” Marks said in a statement. “Ongoing public and private investment has transformed the area into one of the city’s most compelling waterfront markets. bullets: Nalcorp and Clipper Equity acquired 2015 Boardwalk West oceanfront land parcel, Coney Island, for $20M; 69,530 SF with 247 ft Boardwalk frontage.
Site permits filed 2024 for 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use building; part of larger 2006 City Investment Fund acquisition (subdivided into six tax lots).
Coney Island waterfront attracting institutional development capital; limited oceanfront supply.
stories.summary: New York-based developers Nalcorp and Clipper Equity acquired a 69,530-square-foot oceanfront parking lot at 2015 Boardwalk West in Coney Island, Brooklyn, for $20 million from Bath Site LLC. The parcel includes 247 feet of Boardwalk frontage and is part of a larger development on which permits were filed in 2024 for a 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use building. The larger site has been subdivided from a 2006 acquisition by City Investment Fund.
stories.impact: Coney Island oceanfront waterfront remains prime multifamily development ground with limited supply and strong market appetite (demonstrated by $20M land acquisition). Institutional capital targeting beachfront mixed-use signals long-term confidence in Brooklyn waterfront demand and rents; competition for adjacent parcels will intensify, raising land costs and reducing absorption risk for near-term completions. Developers should expedite entitlements and permitting on comparable Coney Island sites to capture rising rents and reduce land hold costs.

stories.title: Survey: 61% of Investors Hold Negative Multifamily Outlook in 2026, Per Berkadia
stories.excerpt: Housing isn’t making anyone happy these days. In a survey of more than 100 principals and executives across private real estate investment firms, Berkadia found that 61 percent of respondents characterized their outlook for the multifamily market in the second half of 2026 as negative due to capital markets volatility, Commercial Observer can first report. Meanwhile, 52 percent said that the asset class performed worse in the first half of the year than they had anticipated. “Six months ago, investors were very optimistic that [volatility] was going to fade and transaction activity was going to accelerate,” said Josh Bodin, senior vice president of capital markets strategy and trading at Berkadia, in a conversation with CO. “Instead, the operating environment has remained a lot more uncertain, interest rate volatility has persisted and property performance has stayed softer than expected,” he added. Bond yields have been high for most of 2026. The 10-Year Treasury currently sits at 4.7 percent, its highest levels since 2023, while the 30-Year Treasury sits at 5.2 percent, a 20-year high. In a separate report, CBRE found that first-quarter investment sales in multifamily hit $29.5 billion, a 6 percent decline year-over-year, while the second quarter saw a rebound of investment sales activity to $34.9 billion (that total was still down by 2.7 percent year-over-year). However, Bodin emphasized these metrics and investors’ sentiments haven’t translated into a loss of confidence in multifamily as an asset class, but has instead changed how investors view execution risk. To this end, Berkadia’s survey found that 82 percent of investors plan to expand their portfolios in the coming months and that 83 percent expect market conditions to improve by late 2027. “On the tailwinds side, near-term, supply deliveries are beginning to moderate in many markets, capital remains really available for well-positioned assets and investors increasingly expect conditions to improve,” said
bullets: Berkadia survey: 61% of multifamily investors hold negative 2H 2026 outlook; 52% say 1H performance worse than expected.
Capital markets volatility, interest rate uncertainty, and softer-than-expected property performance driving investor caution.
10-Year Treasury at 4.7%, 30-Year at 5.2% (20-year high); bond yields remain elevated.
stories.summary: In a Berkadia survey of over 100 real estate investment principals, 61 percent expressed a negative outlook for multifamily in the second half of 2026, citing capital markets volatility, persistent interest rate uncertainty, and property performance that has lagged expectations. Fifty-two percent said first-half 2026 performance was worse than anticipated. The 10-Year Treasury is at 4.7 percent and the 30-Year at 5.2 percent, the latter a 20-year high, maintaining financing costs and debt service burdens.
stories.impact: Widespread investor pessimism and persistent rate volatility signal tighter capital availability, higher underwriting hurdle rates (debt yield + equity return requirements), and compressed development feasibility in marginal markets. Developers should expect slower acquisition price discovery, reduced leverage multiples, and extended hold periods. Conversely, this creates opportunity for well-capitalized, patient operators to acquire distressed assets, control land in tight supply markets, and stage deliveries to avoid peak rate/competition windows.

stories.title: St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort Secures $263M Refi After Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has rescued Al Rayyan Tourism Investment Company (ARTIC)’s St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort out of special servicing, supplying a $263 million loan to refinance the oceanfront property. The New York-based lender assumed $188 million in existing debt and added $70 million in new debt backing the 213-room property in Bal Harbour, Fla., north of Miami Beach, according to public mortgage documents, which valued the asset at $311 million. The new financing comes nearly a year after a $188 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan tied to the resort headed to special servicing as the financing was set to mature. Although the loan remained current and the resort maintained a debt service coverage ratio above break-even, its cash flow in 2024 was about half of 2021 levels, the year it had secured the debt. The lender, Column Financial, wanted ARTIC to buy a replacement interest rate cap, which it had yet to secure, Morningstar reported. ARTIC, which is run by a member of the Qatari ruling family, had purchased the resort for $213 million in 2014, three years after it was completed. The complex, which features three 27-story towers at 9703 Collins Avenue, houses two pools, a 14,000-square-foot spa, five dining outposts, 13,000 square feet of event space as well as a condo component. The hotel owner and condo owners have sparred. In 2024, the condo association sued ARTIC over alleged building defects, safety hazards, and financial mismanagement. The parties settled the suit a year later. Fortress Investment Group and ARTIC did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Fortress Investment Group refinanced Al Rayyan Tourism Investment Company's St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort with $263M loan; property valued $311M.
Fortress assumed $188M existing CMBS debt, added $70M new debt; property exited special servicing after 2024 cash flow collapse.
Hospitality asset cash flow halved year-over-year (2024 vs. 2021); debt service coverage ratio stressed but current.
stories.summary: Fortress Investment Group rescued the St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort from special servicing with a $263 million refinancing that assumed $188 million in existing CMBS debt and added $70 million in new capital, valuing the 213-room oceanfront property at $311 million. The prior $188 million CMBS loan headed to special servicing as it matured, despite the resort remaining current on payments; 2024 cash flow was approximately half 2021 levels. The original lender required the borrower to purchase an interest rate cap, which triggered the workout.
stories.impact: Hospitality distress in luxury waterfront markets (Miami area) reflects post-pandemic normalization and interest rate pressure on debt service; however, Fortress's rescue indicates institutional capital is available to backstop quality assets. Multifamily developers in South Florida should monitor hospitality conversion opportunities (mixed-use, branded residences) and ensure debt structures include rate caps or floating-rate hedges to avoid similar cash flow shocks; high debt service coverage requirements may pressure development pro formas and reduce starts in competitive secondary markets.

stories.title: First Pioneer Properties Buys Queens Retail Center for $24M
stories.excerpt: New York-based real estate management and development firm First Pioneer Properties, along with ABS Partners Real Estate, has acquired a Queens retail center from Levy Properties for $23.5 million, property records made public Thursday show. The one-story property at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside is currently home to an urgent care medical office and Bebeang Baby Store. Jennifer Markowitz of Levy Properties signed the deal for the seller, while Suresh Sani, owner of First Pioneer Properties, signed for the buyers. ABS seems to act as a frequent co-investor and partner of First Pioneer Properties. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. The buyers and seller did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. The property has 24,000 square feet of built space and 74,350 square feet of additional air rights for a total of 98,478 buildable square feet, according to data from PincusCo. The buyers’ intentions for the property are unclear, but Queens has been awash with multifamily developments lately. This month, Wells Fargo provided a $175 million construction loan to the Domain Companies for a 429-unit mixed-income housing development at 35-45, 35-33 and 35-42 41st Street in Astoria. Also this month, LMXD and BedRock Real Estate Partners closed on a $250 million loan to build a housing development at 35-10 Steinway Street in Astoria. Earlier this summer, another Queens retail property changed hands when Punia & Marx Real Estate sold the Whitestone Shopping Center at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway for $56 million. Meanwhile, a historic Queens bowling alley — Whitestone Lanes — at 30-05 Whitestone Expressway in Flushing — sold for $45 million in June as part of a major multifamily development project coming to the area. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: First Pioneer Properties & ABS Partners acquired Queens retail center (213-04 Northern Boulevard, Bayside) for $23.5M; 24,000 SF built, 74,350 SF air rights.
One-story property with urgent care medical office and Bebeang Baby Store; total 98,478 buildable SF.
Queens experiencing multifamily development surge; air rights and land-banking potential signal redevelopment optionality.
stories.summary: New York-based First Pioneer Properties and ABS Partners acquired a one-story retail center at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside, Queens, for $23.5 million. The property includes 24,000 square feet of built space and 74,350 square feet of air rights for 98,478 total buildable square feet, currently home to an urgent care medical office and Bebeang Baby Store. The buyers' development intentions were not disclosed, though Queens has seen a surge in multifamily activity.
stories.impact: Acquisition of low-density Queens retail with substantial air rights signals developer optionality to convert/redevelop to higher-density multifamily, reflecting tight supply and strong rents in Queens (Bayside, Flushing corridors). Strategic land-banking and entitlement for mixed-use multifamily redevelopment on low-cost retail foundations creates value capture opportunity; similar properties in transit-accessible outer-borough locations are prime conversion targets as Queens rents compress gap to Manhattan/Brooklyn.
